welcome_lead: Three classic recursive patterns every CS student must know.

final_note: Pattern recognition is most of recursion.

concepts.def: n! = n times (n-1)! with base case 0! = 1.
Visit root, then left, then right.
Visit left, then root, then right.
Visit left, then right, then root.

walkthroughs.body_html: n! = n times (n-1)!, with 0! = 1. The recursive call shrinks by 1 each time and stops at the base case 0.
Naive recursive Fibonacci is O(2^n) because each call branches twice. Memoisation stores F(k) once computed, dropping it to O(n).
On a binary tree: pre-order (NLR), in-order (LNR — sorted on BSTs), post-order (LRN — useful for deletion). All naturally expressed by recursion.
